recent_posts.title: Glitch web development platform shuts down project hosting
recent_posts.summary: Glitch, a popular web development platform that made building websites accessible and fun, has officially ended its project hosting services. The team shared farewell messages highlighting how Glitch removed barriers to web development, allowing anyone to create and deploy projects easily. Users can still access their dashboards to download projects or set redirects until early 2026.

recent_posts.title: Glitch ends web hosting service in July 2025
recent_posts.summary: Glitch is shutting down its web hosting service on July 8, 2025, ending support for millions of hosted applications. Users will have access to download their code through the end of 2025, with new redirect features to maintain existing URLs. The decision stems from rising operational costs and the emergence of superior hosting alternatives like Fly.io, Deno, and Netlify. Current Glitch Pro subscriptions will be refunded, and the company is preparing migration guides to help users transition to other platforms.

recent_posts.title: Winter 2025 on Glitch: Little of this, little of that
recent_posts.summary: Winter of 2025 on Glitch showcases a variety of unique and creative apps developed by the Glitch community, celebrating winners from 2024 and highlighting interesting projects such as interactive VR scenes, innovative UX designs, and fun games. Readers are encouraged to explore these apps and participate in the Glitch community by sharing their own creations.

recent_posts.title: Do you remember why we named this thing Glitch?
recent_posts.summary: The author reflects on Glitch's journey, highlights the challenges of maintaining a long-standing platform, and emphasizes the importance of reconnecting with the community. The post discusses the evolving developer ecosystem, the technical debt accumulated over the years, and the inspiration drawn from newer platforms. The essence of Glitch as a platform that embraces imperfection and creativity is reaffirmed, with a call for community support during the evolution ahead.

recent_posts.title: Fall 2024 on Glitch, Part 2
recent_posts.summary: Take a moment to embrace rest as we head into the new year, and explore various ways the Glitch Community has showcased their creativity this fall. The post highlights several impressive projects created by different users on Glitch, including portfolio sites, shelters for hurricane victims, games, and tools. It also announces upcoming nominations for the 'Last Year on Glitch' celebration.

recent_posts.title: Fall 2024 on Glitch, Part 1
recent_posts.summary: Highlights from the Glitch community, including a variety of innovative projects like a movie catalog app, a Rubik's cube game, and map-based applications. Improvements to the Glitch editor's drag-and-drop feature and a spotlight on a tutorial for enhancing your site with a Free Fastly Developer account. Don't miss the recap of the Glitch Community Code Jams and the sneak peek at a nostalgic project, How did you find me?

recent_posts.title: A new update makes the Glitch editor more convenient than ever
recent_posts.summary: Glitch has updated its editor to allow drag-and-drop for any file or entire folders, significantly improving convenience. Instructors can now easily upload projects for students to remix and see live on the Internet. Bugs around file renaming have been fixed, and file management has undergone several enhancements, including easier file movement within the project tree.

recent_posts.title: August 2024 on Glitch: Award winning
recent_posts.summary: August featured several noteworthy projects on Glitch, including games, virtual avatars, and tools to enhance creativity. Highlights include 'subdue-them', '3d-icon-maouh', and 'kamala hive' inspired projects. The theme for September's Code Jam is 'maps', and there are new tutorial videos by Sue Smith for using Glitch with Fastly. Additionally, a Glitch project won significant recognition from both the Girl Scouts organization and a state senate for its impact on climate crisis action.

recent_posts.title: Fancify your website user experience with edge computing
recent_posts.summary: Over the past months, various free Fastly services to enhance Glitch sites have been introduced. This post highlights using edge computing with Fastly Compute to significantly improve user experience. It provides a guide to deploying a Fastly Compute app on Glitch with a single command and demonstrates additional ways to enhance website UX at the edge, such as password protection and synthetic content creation.

recent_posts.title: July 2024 on Glitch: The jams come in waves
recent_posts.summary: July 2024 was packed with exciting events and new projects for the Glitch community. The Glitch Speaker Series launched with Alondra Nelson discussing ethical and practical applications of AI. The month’s standout project was ~kamala-holding-vinyls, a meme generator gaining widespread attention. Glitch will also be hosting Art + Code at the final XOXO event in Portland. Several other creative projects were highlighted, including ~bumper-frogger, ~woolen-treasure-novel, and ~tanabata-wish. The Glitch Community Code Jams continue to inspire with July's theme of 'waves' and an upcoming prompt to 'just draw.'
